title: Is the OpenRAM access energy in SKY130 liberty files an energy at all, and does accel-pdkprice's weight-stationary verdict survive?
lede: OpenRAM's clk0 figure is an average power in mW over one cycle of an unstated period, not pJ: the unpacked verdict (register-file WS wins) holds for any period above 3 ns, while the packed verdict flips between 1 and 31 ns, so accel-pdkprice's packed conclusion is conditional
summary: accel-pdkprice read the clk0 internal_power of four OpenRAM SRAM macros as pJ per access. Reading the generator source at a pinned commit (five tested facts) shows the value is an average power in mW over exactly one clock cycle, so the access energy is the value times the characterisation period T, which the shipped files do not give (their minimum_period reads 0.09 to 0.1 ns, not usable). Sweeping T = 0.1 to 20 ns over the 64 cells of accel-pdkprice (it reproduces all 64 verdicts at 1 ns): with one weight per access, register-file weight-stationary beats output-stationary in all 32 cells from 3 ns up; with weights packed it wins 0 of 32 at 0.5 ns, 6 at 2, 17 at 5 and 29 at 20 ns (flip periods 0.8 to 31 ns). Partial sums in SRAM lose at every T because the scale cancels. Library values read from source, not a measurement; T is swept, not sourced, because no file gives it; the shipped libraries may predate the pinned source.
